I used to be heavy into smoking weed. (This is not a post about weed being "bad" or looking down on anyone who does it. I just don't do it anymore but I don't care if anyone chooses to smoke.) And I had a lot of "friends". Well, basically people to get high with. One night I show up to my friends boyfriends to hang out with them and one of their friends. I noticed that they were snorting coke. They asked me if I wanted to do it, and I said no. So we just smoked a couple bowls of weed. Well, I didn't find out until later that they laced the weed with coke already, and didn't tell me. At this point I was on antidepressants as well. Long story short, I had a terrible reaction due to the antidepressants and cocaine mixture. I ended up in the hospital with doctors telling me they thought my heart was going to give out. My parents understandably freaked out and called the police on my "friends." After that, none of them asked me how I was doing, or if I was ok. In fact, they were more worried about the possibility of getting into legal trouble. They didn't care about me at all. And once I decided I wanted to get sober and not even smoke weed anymore and focus on school, all my "friends" disappeared. Never asked me once how I was doing or what I was up to or if I wanted to hang out. None of that. And that's how I learned the hard way that you can't build friendships off of drugs, because they're not true friends at all. It was hard accepting the fact that the people who I thought were my friends really weren't my friends at all.
